events.note: 1647: the Ottomans take the Cretan countryside; Venice keeps Candia, Siteia and the island fortresses of Souda, Spinalonga and Gramvousa. Same event as republic-of-venice/ledger/122, which is skipped because the gazetteer has no place 'Souda'. Cretan War page: the Ottomans went 'to conquer the eastern half of the island, except for the fortress of Siteia' (1647) and 'By the beginning of 1648, all of Crete, except Candia and a few strongholds like the island of Gramvousa, was in Ottoman hands'; the 1669 terms name 'the isolated island fortresses of Spinalonga, Gramvousa and Souda', which Venice therefore still held. Souda is given here by coordinates. [Review 2 Nov 2026: caption sentence added. The Souda point falls in the grid cell that also holds Chania's point (24.09 E, 35.56 N); Souda Bay page: 'The Venetians managed to hold on to the strategic islands within Souda Bay until 1715'. This event pushes the Ottoman 1648 snap over its tolerance; keyframe_overrides/5 keeps rural Crete Ottoman in 1648.]

region.text: Kutai Kartanegara after the 1635 merger with Martadipura: the Mahakam core and a 30 km disc round Muara Kaman

events.note: Kutai Kartanegara holds the lower Mahakam and Muara Kaman, capital of Kutai Martadipura, which Aji Pangeran Sinum Panji Mendapa (ruled 1635-1650) conquered, merging the two realms. Stand-in for the 1635 annexation (kutai-kingdom/ledger/1) and the 1635-1647 keyframe, which resolve to nothing because the gazetteer lacks 'Muara Kaman' (and 'Kutai Lama' for the 1300-1634 keyframe): the state has no land at the 1640 anchor. Kutai page: Aji Pangeran Sinum Panji Mendapa, who ruled 1635-1650, 'was able to conquer the kingdom of Kutai Martadipura and merged the two realms'; 'Its capital is believed to be the current Muara Kaman district'; the sultanate lasts to 1844. Dated 1640, the first year of this window, because 1635-1639 belong to the previous window. [Review 2 Nov 2026: caption sentence added.]

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's shape (Cliopatria 1642 plus Beijing) holds only 517 of Shaanxi's 965 cells, so 419 Shaanxi cells (Xi'an and the north) fall to nobody for 1644 and come back in 1645. The page: 'Li Zicheng fled to Xi'an' after Beijing, Dorgon sent armies 'in October of that year, ... to expel Li Zicheng from his stronghold in Shaanxi', 'forcing Li Zicheng to abandon his headquarters in Xi'an in February 1645'. Shaanxi stays Shun through 1644.

keyframe_overrides.why: Added by the reviewer. Cliopatria's 1648 Ottoman shape lacks most of rural Crete; with events/1 the Ottomans hold two more cells outside it, the 1648 snap passes its 20-cell tolerance and releases 12 rural Cretan cells to nobody in 1648-1649 (8 that kingdom-of-candia/ledger/7 gives the Ottomans that year) and adds 5 cells round Novigrad, which Venice retook in 1647. The page: 'By the beginning of 1648, all of Crete, except Candia and a few strongholds like the island of Gramvousa, was in Ottoman hands.' With Crete in the shape the snap stays within tolerance (trial: no Ottoman snap in 1648; all rural Crete Ottoman in 1648-1649). The keyframe runs 1648-1661 but snaps only in 1648.

rulings.why: In 1644 the size rule gives Zhang Xianzhong's Xi 438 Kham cells (Garze and Aba, 97.5-101.8 E, 28.8-33.9 N) that Tibet, the Khoshut vassal, holds from 1642, because the Xi keyframes (1644, and 1645-1646 without Chongqing) are the whole Ming province of Sichuan; the ruling runs to 1646, when the Xi leave Sichuan (October), because with 1644 alone the cells pass to Xi in 1645 and to nobody in 1646-47. The page: 'In the winter of 1640-1641, Güshi crushed the king of Beri, Donyo Dorje' (Kham), 'With the taking of Shigatse in 1642, Güshi had brought all of Tibet under the control of the Gelug school', and 'Güshi's title as king of Ü-Tsang and Kham' (1653); it says nothing of Zhang Xianzhong or Sichuan. The Xi page says only that the Xi 'ruled most of Sichuan province'.
